name: get_type_attr_as_size
reason: getTypeAttrAsSize/asSsize mirror the 3.15.2 body (:30-41: the lookup's own error returned as is, the new PyErr_Occurred branch, the "Missed attribute" TypeError, then PyLong_AsSsize_t with its non-int TypeError and OverflowError, Objects/longobject.c:708-751 checked), and sizeOrNull is the callers' n < 0 test; SizeReadSpec pins every case of the dict's content, including the negative int that returns -1 with nothing set, which typeobj-structseq-new-sets-exception refutes with a bug record reproducing on 3.15.2 and main.

name: get_real_size
reason: realSize is Py_SIZE + (tp_basicsize - 32) / 8; the Nat subtraction matches the signed C because every type that finishes construction has tp_basicsize >= 32 (check_basicsize_includes_size_and_offsets for NewType, the match_args crash before any static type with n_in_sequence > n_members is usable); NewIndexContract pins realSize = n on the honest layout, and the replace and reduce refutations run it.

name: PyStructSequence_New
reason: pssNew reads n_fields then n_sequence_fields, allocates through gcNewVar (the size_t wrap and rounding of _PyObject_VAR_SIZE, Include/cpython/objimpl.h:22-26, cited as 23-27, and gc_alloc's PY_SSIZE_T_MAX - presize refusal, Python/gc.c:2012-2028, both checked), resets the hash word, sets Py_SIZE and NULLs n_fields slots; NewIndexContract pins both allocator outcomes and the exact block on every honest type, NewReadsFirst pins that a failing read decides the result before any allocation, and the NULL-without-exception path is refuted with a bug record.

name: PyStructSequence_SetItem
reason: pssSetItem is the release-build store with the asserts compiled out; NewIndexContract proves that on a fresh honest object every documented index 0 <= i < n_fields is written alone (read back, every other index unchanged) and that i < 0 or past the block is undefined behaviour, which a constant or neighbour-clobbering SetItem would fail.

name: PyStructSequence_GetItem
reason: pssGetItem is the unchecked borrowed read of a release build; NewIndexContract pins it to return exactly what SetItem stored at every documented index and undefined behaviour outside the block, and ReprShape uses it for the item reads of structseq_repr.

name: structseq_traverse
reason: The no-behaviour reason applies under the stated GC traversal policy: the body visits the heap type and the get_real_size items and returns 0.

name: structseq_dealloc
reason: The no-behaviour reason applies under the stated tp_dealloc policy: it untracks, XDECREFs the get_real_size items (gh-122527 comment checked), frees the block and DECREFs a heap type; it calls no PyObject_ClearWeakRefs (a field named __weaklistoffset__ is refused with SystemError by special_offset_from_member, typeobject.c:5277-5283, since the members are _Py_T_OBJECT) and runs no finalizer itself. Its reads past the block for objects whose Py_SIZE disagrees with the allocation follow from the already-refuted size-attribute paths.

name: structseq_new_impl
reason: newImplC folds the two PyDict_GET_SIZE(dict) reads (:238 and :255) into one fixed CDictArg.size, though the lookups between them can run a key's __eq__ that empties or grows the dict (a key hashing like 'tm_zone' whose __eq__ calls d.clear() makes CPython return all-None fields where the model raises "got duplicate or unexpected field name(s)"), and the only functional theorem, ReduceRoundTrip, is over the separate StructSeq.lean model whose argument is a plain list that cannot raise and which reads no size attributes, so the length checks, the not-a-dict refusal and the unexpected-name TypeError are pinned by no theorem (the C mirror carries only the NewImplInBounds refutation).

name: structseq_repr
reason: structseqRepr computes prealloc = strlen(tp_name) + 1 + Py_SIZE * 5 + 1 (:281-282) in unbounded Int and its writer (UnicodeObj/ObjectWriter.lean) cannot fail to allocate, so ReprShape's "for every object" is false on CPython for Py_SIZE around 2^35 and above, which copy.replace reaches after time.struct_time.n_sequence_fields = 2**40: PyUnicodeWriter_Create (Objects/unicode_writer.c:105-132) raises MemoryError (past 2^61 the Py_ssize_t product overflows to a negative length and ValueError) where the theorem predicts the SystemError at the tp_members sentinel; the item __repr__ failure path is mirrored, and typeobj-structseq-repr-labels is a well-founded refutation (gh-154387 duplicate).

name: structseq_reduce
reason: ReduceInBoundsHonest assumes u <= v (HonestLayout), which its registry statement presents as "the size attributes PyStructSequence_NewType stored", but NewType does not enforce it and Doc/c-api/tuple.rst does not state it (only the source comment at :23-24 does): fields [x, unnamed, unnamed] with n_in_sequence = 1 build a type whose __reduce__ reads tp_members[-1] at :369, the interesting case the hypothesis removes; the theorem holds for a reduceC that always raises, and the only functional property, ReduceRoundTrip, runs on the StructSeq.lean structseqReduce, which has none of the failure paths (n_unnamed_fields read, NULL items, member-name decoding).

name: structseq_replace
reason: Both models compare keyword names with pure equality (popKw in StructSeqC.lean, popName in StructSeq.lean), but PyDict_PopString (Objects/dictobject.c:3326-3339) compares an exact str with the kwargs keys, and a str-subclass keyword (copy.replace(t, **{S('tm_year'): 1}), S defining __hash__ = str.__hash__ and an __eq__ that raises) runs Python code that can raise, where ReplaceSpec claims success; ReplaceSpec is also over the abstract model without the size reads, the allocation or the decode failure, and the C mirror's ReplaceInBoundsHonest would hold for a replaceC that always raised.

name: count_members
reason: countMembers is the walk to the terminator counting the PyStructSequence_UnnamedField pointers (pointer comparison modelled by FName.unnamed); countMembers_eq and NewTypeLayout's dict and member conjuncts pin both counts in every build, so a miscount falsifies the theorem, and it has no failure exit; both NewType refutations run it.

name: initialize_members
reason: initMembersLoop mirrors :552-567 (skip unnamed, member k at slot i) and NewTypeLayout pins tp_members = the named fields at their own indices, but only for a newType that succeeded: an initialize_members whose PyMem_NEW always failed, or never failed, satisfies it, and its MemoryError exit (:545-549) appears in no statement.

name: _PyStructSequence_InitBuiltinWithFlags
reason: The internal-bootstrap reason applies: it is declared extern (no PyAPI_FUNC) in Include/internal/pycore_structseq.h under Py_BUILD_CORE, and its only callers (Python/sysmodule.c, Python/thread.c, Python/errors.c, Objects/longobject.c, Objects/floatobject.c, through _PyStructSequence_InitBuiltin) initialise fixed static descs at interpreter start-up.

name: _PyStructSequence_FiniBuiltin
reason: The internal-bootstrap reason applies: extern in the internal header and called only from the finalization of the same static builtin struct sequence types, after which that interpreter runs no Python code against them.

name: _PyStructSequence_NewType
reason: NewTypeLayout constrains only successful builds, so a NewType that always raised satisfies it; nothing states that a valid desc (0 <= n_in_sequence <= #fields, UTF-8 names, allocator and rest succeeding) builds a type, nor pins the TypeError for n_in_sequence = #fields + 1..3 and the SystemError for >= #fields + 5 or < 0 that the refuted entry's source claims; the (int) cast at :775 is conditioned away (hidden < 2^28 - 4) with no refutation on record for the wrap back to a positive wrong basicsize; the tp_flags parameter is not modelled (stated in the notes); the newtype-in-bounds refutation (n_in_sequence = #fields + 4) is sound and has its bug record.

name: PyStructSequence_NewType
reason: The wrapper is newType with no flags, so it inherits the _PyStructSequence_NewType gap: NewTypeLayout says nothing unless the build succeeded, so a PyStructSequence_NewType that always raised satisfies it, and no statement pins when a desc is accepted or which refusal a bad n_in_sequence gets.
